summary:
CrewSafety is a prototype web and iPhone app designed to support astronauts’ safety and wellbeing during space missions.

Camera-based activity monitoring prompts check-ins after prolonged inactivity and can escalate alerts to a trusted crew circle. A shared dashboard displays crew status and safety events, while a manual spacesuit checklist helps users record inspections.

The journal uses Meta MUSE to review entries and provide supportive reflections. After three entries within 14 days, it offers collective observations and practical suggestions based on recurring themes. These reflections support wellbeing without providing medical diagnoses.

Daily care activities connect to an astronaut companion and a virtual space garden, encouraging regular participation.

The app uses JavaScript, SwiftUI, MediaPipe, and Meta MUSE, with its research context informed by NASA human-spaceflight resources.

Future development includes a local LLM, integration with dedicated security cameras, and camera-assisted spacesuit maintenance.
details:
We built CrewSafety to help astronauts look after themselves and each other during long missions. Our prototype brings physical safety checks and mental wellbeing support into one web and iPhone app.

Camera-based activity monitoring prompts a check-in after prolonged inactivity and can alert a trusted crew circle. A shared dashboard shows crew status and safety events, while a manual spacesuit checklist helps record inspections. The journal combines sentiment analysis with Meta MUSE to offer supportive reflections. After three entries within 14 days, it provides collective suggestions based on what the person has written.

We also wanted daily care to feel approachable. An astronaut companion and a virtual space garden connect everyday check-ins with visible progress, giving users a reason to return beyond responding to alerts.

We used JavaScript, Next.js, HTML, CSS, SwiftUI, MediaPipe, ElevenLabs, Twillio, and Meta MUSE, with laptop and iPhone cameras. NASA research informed the project, and we considered privacy, false alarms, user control, and the limits of AI-generated advice.

Our goal is to help crews notice when someone may need support and make reaching out easier. Future development includes a local LLM, dedicated security camera integration, and camera-assisted spacesuit maintenance.
